entries.name: Malgrath, the Rot Beneath
entries.summary: Malgrath is the forbidden god of plague, corruption, famine, poisoned land, spiritual decay, blight, rot-cults, and demon-wound geography. His Moral/Theological Standing is Forbidden Malignant. His symbol is a cracked black root dripping green sickness. Plague cultists, corrupted druids, famine prophets, blight-priests, and wasteland warlocks invoke him where life turns wrong and survival begins to worship decay.

entries.name: Nharvek, the Chain King
entries.summary: Nharvek is the forbidden god of tyranny, coercive rule, soul-binding, fear, and stolen freedom. His Moral/Theological Standing is Forbidden Malignant. His symbol is a black iron chain wrapped around a crown. Tyrants, cruel jailers, corrupt officials, domination cults, and soul-binders invoke him in secret. His cults are malignant because they use fear and supernatural pressure to demand submission.

entries.name: Ossyra, the Knife Behind the Smile
entries.summary: Ossyra is the forbidden goddess of betrayal, murder, false friendship, assassination, poison, secret cults, and treachery wearing a familiar face. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Forbidden Malignant. Her symbol is a smiling mask pierced from behind by a narrow blade. Assassins, poisoners, false companions, court murderers, and secret murder societies invoke her when trust itself is the weapon.

entries.name: Velkora, the Hollow Queen
entries.summary: Velkora is the forbidden goddess of corrupted undeath, lichdom, hollow immortality, blood hunger without restraint, forbidden resurrection, and death refused at the expense of others. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Forbidden Malignant. Her symbol is a pale crown above an open grave. Necromancers, liches, corpse-cults, cruel vampires, grief-broken nobles, and rulers terrified of death may turn to her, but she does not represent all undead or all vampires.

entries.name: Ardoval, the Oath-Crowned
entries.summary: Ardoval is Valenreach's benefactor god of oaths, crowns, rightful rule, inheritance, courts, sworn duty, guardianship, and noble burden. His Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent, though critics warn that his temples can protect old privilege when law is treated as holier than mercy. His symbol is a crowned sword laid across an open oath-ring. Kings, judges, knights, nobles, officers, and heirs invoke him before coronations, verdicts, contracts, marriages, and battlefield vows.

entries.name: Auraleth, the Sky-Bound Oath
entries.summary: Auraleth is the Cloudspire Dominion's benefactor god of cliffs, wind bridges, storm beacons, griffin riders, falling risks, lift-rights, sky roads, balance, engineering courage, and promises made where the ground cannot protect you. Auraleth's Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent. The symbol is a white knot tied around a feather and iron hook. Cloud monasteries, bridge engineers, griffin riders, cliff cities, sky couriers, and storm-watchers honor Auraleth because one broken rope can become murder.

entries.name: Bravik, the Hammer Saint
entries.summary: Bravik is the god of forge, craft, stonework, mines, fortresses, honest labor, builders, smiths, endurance, shieldwalls, and properly made things. His Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent. His symbol is a hammer laid across an anvil-stone. Dwarves, smiths, miners, masons, armorers, soldiers, engineers, and workers honor him when a thing must hold under weight, fire, time, or war.

entries.name: Dravok, the Iron Will
entries.summary: Dravok is the Dreadmark Dominion's benefactor god of discipline, conquest, punishment, command, pain, obedience, and survival through strength. His Moral/Theological Standing is Controversial Patron: Dreadmark reveres him as the god who makes order possible, while most other nations fear his worship as a path to tyranny. His symbol is a black gauntlet gripping a broken spear. His priests bless legions, punish deserters, and teach that weakness becomes cruelty when it cannot defend what it claims to love.

entries.name: Khorvash, the Thunderhoof
entries.summary: Khorvash is the Fangbound Clans' benefactor god of mounted clans, herd rights, raids, monster hunts, strength, challenge, migration, kinship, and proof of worth. His Moral/Theological Standing is Accepted Necessary. His symbol is a hoofprint split by lightning. Orcish holds, beastkin families, riders, clan chiefs, hunters, herders, and raiding bands honor him through contests, oaths over herds, challenges, and victories earned in open sight.

entries.name: Lythirien, the Root of Memory
entries.summary: Lythirien is the Lythael Elven Dominion's benefactor goddess of memory, forests, beauty, ancestral continuity, living history, restraint, and old songs. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent. Her symbol is a white tree with silver roots. Elves, historians, singers, druids, artists, and ancestral guardians honor her in living groves and root-vaults where memory is sung, not merely recorded.

entries.name: Maelthar, the Storm-Bearer
entries.summary: Maelthar is the Tide Empire's benefactor god of sea, storms, endurance, voyages, shipwrecks, cold courage, and return from hardship. His Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent: he is respected and prayed to, but never treated as gentle. His symbol is a black wave beneath a silver star. Sailors, admirals, fishers, raiders, explorers, shipwrights, and coastal soldiers ask him for strength to endure the storm rather than escape it.

entries.name: Myrathis, the Veiled Flame
entries.summary: Myrathis is the Arcanum Ascendancy's benefactor goddess of magic, hidden knowledge, controlled study, transformation, arcane law, dangerous discovery, and secrecy with purpose. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Controversial Patron. Her symbol is a violet flame behind a half-mask. Mages, scholars, archivists, alchemists, occultists, and ambitious students honor her in libraries, laboratories, sealed lecture halls, and observatories where knowledge is treated as power with cost.

entries.name: Neryssan, the Coral Crown
entries.summary: Neryssan is the Coral Throne's benefactor goddess of reef law, sea courts, tide obligations, ocean spirits, submerged sovereignty, pearl tribute, and old marine pacts. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent. Her symbol is a coral crown circled by three tide-lines. Sea nobles, reef judges, merfolk envoys, tide-priests, pearl houses, and coastal diplomats honor her when sea-law, alliance, and obligation matter more than dryland custom.

entries.name: Noctheris, the Crimson Guest
entries.summary: Noctheris is the Nightglass Principality's benefactor god of invitation, blood debt, restrained hunger, vampire etiquette, night courts, immortal memory, predatory courtesy, and hospitality with teeth. His Moral/Theological Standing is Controversial Patron. His symbol is a crimson cup beneath a closed black parasol. Restrained vampires, blood-law judges, night courtiers, mortal treaty families, and conflicted immortals honor him as the power that teaches hunger must answer to law.

entries.name: Sahekir, the Brass Horizon
entries.summary: Sahekir is the desert benefactor god of sun-waste cultures, glass roads, caravans, mirages, oases, water-rights, heat endurance, brass astronomy, and horizon omens. His Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent. His symbol is a brass sun half-buried in a horizon line. Desert rulers, caravan masters, water judges, astronomer-priests, guides, and oasis families honor him because survival, hospitality, and water are sacred law beneath the burning sky.

entries.name: Serrava, the Open Hand
entries.summary: Serrava is the Solmire Concord's benefactor goddess of trade, roads, diplomacy, contracts, hospitality, neutral ground, river passage, and fair exchange. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent: she protects bargains and guest-right, but she is not sentimental. Her symbol is an open hand marked with a coin and road-line. Merchants, diplomats, innkeepers, caravan guards, messengers, negotiators, and river traders invoke her before deals and journeys.

entries.name: Solcaris, the Unblinking Sun
entries.summary: Solcaris is the Solarian Theocracy's benefactor god of sun, truth, healing, judgment, revelation, purification, public virtue, and righteous fire. His Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent, Controversial in Practice. His symbol is a golden eye within a sunburst. His worship heals the innocent and exposes corruption, but becomes dangerous when zealots decide that doubt is sin, privacy is corruption, and fire is the only honest cure.

entries.name: Thalyra, the Pearl-Warden
entries.summary: Thalyra is the Stormpearl Isles' benefactor goddess of island councils, pearl houses, storm signs, lighthouse rites, fishing fleets, boat law, free captains, and weather-wise survival. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Ambivalent. Her symbol is a white pearl held inside a storm-ring. Islanders invoke her before voyages, elections, storm seasons, harbor judgments, and disputes where freedom must still answer to the sea.

entries.name: Veyrasha, the Unbound Flame
entries.summary: Veyrasha is the Emberhorn Accord's benefactor goddess of pacts, ambition, self-mastery, chosen identity, renaming, emancipation, and freedom from inherited damnation. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Controversial Patron. Her symbol is a red flame breaking a black chain. Civilized demons, pact-makers, exiles, rebels, and oath-breakers seeking rebirth honor her as the power that says birth does not decide destiny, but every choice binds the soul.

entries.name: Caelwyn, the First Song
entries.summary: Caelwyn is the deity of art, music, love, inspiration, beauty, performance, festivals, courtly romance, public memory, and stories that outlive witnesses. Caelwyn's Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent. The symbol is a golden harp-string crossing an open mouth. Bards, lovers, actors, poets, courtiers, festival keepers, mourners, and historians honor Caelwyn when feeling must become song, vow, play, or legend.

entries.name: Elaris, the Silver Veil
entries.summary: Elaris is the goddess of moon, dreams, prophecy, omens, hidden roads, fate-glimpses, nightmares, sleepwalking, and warnings no one fully understands. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Accepted Ambivalent. Her symbol is a silver veil drawn across a crescent moon. Seers, midwives, travelers by night, dream-readers, hidden pilgrims, and frightened rulers honor her when signs arrive indirectly and truth refuses to stand in daylight.

entries.name: Hestrelle, the Gentle Hearth
entries.summary: Hestrelle is the common goddess of hearth, mercy, healing, childbirth, refuge, food, wells, family, rural prosperity, and ordinary kindness. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Revered Benevolent. Her symbol is a clay lamp cupped between two hands. Families, healers, midwives, cooks, farmers, refugees, village priests, and the poor honor her in kitchens, sickrooms, birthing houses, roadside shelters, and any place where a stranger is given warmth.

entries.name: Morcant, the Last Witness
entries.summary: Morcant is the god of death, funerals, ancestors, graves, last rites, ghosts, oathbound dead, buried memory, final testimony, and proper endings. His Moral/Theological Standing is Accepted Necessary. His symbol is a closed eye above a black candle. Gravekeepers, mourners, executioners, ancestor-priests, old soldiers, ghost hunters, Mourning Bell Wardens, and communities living near the Blackbell Deadroads honor him because death must be witnessed, named, and given rest.

entries.name: Nysera, the Turning Coin
entries.summary: Nysera is the goddess of luck, chance, thieves, gamblers, sudden reversals, wagers, escapes, lost causes, and survival by wit. Her Moral/Theological Standing is Accepted Ambivalent. Her symbol is a two-faced coin spinning above a dagger point. Rogues, gamblers, smugglers, desperate travelers, rebels, outlaws, and merchants in dangerous markets honor her because fortune is neither fair nor evil, only turning.

entries.name: Tharvane, the Wild Horn
entries.summary: Tharvane is the god of beasts, monsters, forests, hunting, livestock, seasons, predator and prey, wild fertility, and territory beyond court law. His Moral/Theological Standing is Accepted Necessary. His symbol is a stag skull crowned with green leaves. Rangers, hunters, druids, beast-tamers, frontier villages, monster clans, and awakened creatures honor him because civilization is never separate from the world it cuts, burns, eats, and fears.

entries.name: Vaunthis, the Nameless Door
entries.summary: Vaunthis is the god of exile, forbidden thresholds, lost paths, erased names, vanished cities, dangerous crossings, and doors that should not open. His Moral/Theological Standing is Feared but Recognized. His symbol is a blank door without handle or hinge. Exiles, forbidden pilgrims, vanished cults, boundary-mages, and those who seek hidden places know his signs, though most temples treat his worship with caution rather than open devotion.
